## Content research and reproducibility

- Candidate: **Why an active AgentSight host is not a running conversation**. Reader decision: interpret a running-session count separately from a live host/helper process count and avoid mistaking a sticky session association for ongoing work. Proposed canonical slug `/blog/why-agentsight-running-sessions-differ-from-live-processes/` (not published).
- Current catalog/sitemap and existing articles checked: progressive fleet article answers refresh latency; normalization article explains path/sticky/CWD matching broadly; audit provenance article answers field lineage and non-comparable confidence; native discovery answers enumeration; top counters answers summary-source selection. New reader question concerns activity classification and resource counting across shared hosts, not rephrasing these. Link to those pages rather than duplicating their explanations.
- [Exact product PR #273](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/pull/273) and [process matcher](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/2b16f697f557a8694e423ccf96d9cd5908222c91/ext/session/src/process_match.rs): candidate collection no longer mutates sticky binding state; candidate ordering prioritizes session end recency, then confidence, then input indices; the greedy selection consumes each root PID and session ID once. This is not a global optimal matching or proof that all simultaneous conversations are separately attributed. Fixture two open Codex logs, old sorting first, new wins. Distinguish this **unreleased master** behavior from v1.0.35.
- [sessionState.mjs](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/2b16f697f557a8694e423ccf96d9cd5908222c91/ext/web/lib/sessionState.mjs): executed standalone Node v22.16.0 test of the extracted exact predicate bodies with a fixed synthetic clock; seven assertions passed. Positive PID and nonempty session ID: timestamp age 179999 ms -> true; 180000 ms -> false; one hour in future -> true; missing timestamp -> true; invalid timestamp -> true; null session ID -> false; null PID -> false. This is a predicate-level experiment, not a full product/UI run or measured user behavior. A recent transcript, clock skew or fallback can therefore produce a running badge without proof of ongoing computation.
- [fleetData.test.mjs](https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/agentsight/blob/2b16f697f557a8694e423ccf96d9cd5908222c91/ext/web/lib/fleetData.test.mjs): one session plus two helper rows yields one running session, four processes, 8 summed CPU percentage points, 150 MB summed RSS (synthetic fixture).
